messages:
Raj - Sales: FYI incoming from AuroraHealth. They want a Dedicated pool for real-time ECG analysis. Ask: 30 GPUs baseline, up to 100 GPUs burst 2x/day for 10–15 min. p95 inference <200ms. Pricing + MRC request.
Emma - Product: thanks. do we have their expected sustained qps and payload sizes? p95 200ms on 7B is tight. any model details?
Raj - Sales: they mentioned an internal model (open-ecg-7b) — typically batch=1, seq~1024, ~400 tokens per request. sessions are long-lived, lots of KV reuse. sustained qps ~120 req/s, bursts to 1.2k req/s during morning windows.
Sophie - Solutions Eng: confirms batch=1, KV-cache will help for sessions but bursts are mostly new sessions. model uses 4-bit quant. latency target depends on GPU type — on A10G/A100 we can hit ~150ms p95 for 7B if optimized, but depends on throughput.
Sam - Eng Runtime: continuous batching helps for throughput but for p95<200ms at 1.2k qps we need parallelism across GPUs + small max_batch_size, and KV cache locality. Suggest two model variants: 
- "latency-optimized": lower seq len prefilling, tuned kernels, higher GPU reservation.
- "cost-optimized": denser packing, slightly higher latency.
Sam - Eng Runtime: also we should consider quantization to 4-bit + Triton kernels. without that hitting their p95 at peak will be expensive.
Li - Eng Infra: for autoscaling, Dedicated supports reserved baseline + burst capacity. We can do: reserve 30 GPUs in pool, allow burst to 100 via pooled burst policy (cross-customer) or reserved temp nodes. Need finance ok for cost+MRC implications. Also need to confirm region (they're EU).
Maria - Customer Success: AuroraHealth is regulated — they need VPC deployment + audit logs and SOC2 support. Private control plane requested. That affects where bursts can come from (on-prem vs cloud).
Emma - Product: key questions for sales to confirm with customer: 1) strictness of p95 SLA (will they accept degradation during extreme bursts?), 2) willingness to accept two-tier model variants, 3) commitment length for reserved capacity.
Raj - Sales: I'll ask. they prefer hard SLOs for clinical use but may accept canary window for rollout. Commit term likely 12–24 months if pricing is right.
Sophie - Solutions Eng: also ask about model drift / frequent model updates. If they push new weights often, rollout tooling and canary capacity are required.
Sam - Eng Runtime: quick config sketch for autoscale policy (narrow example):
```yaml
pool: aurorahealth-dedicated
baseline_gpus: 30
burst_limit_gpus: 100
burst_duration_minutes: 15
scale_policy:
  metric: requests_per_gpu
  target: 4   # ~4 qps per GPU for low-latency profile
  cooldown: 60s
fallbacks:
  - model_variant: latency-optimized
  - model_variant: cost-optimized
```
Li - Eng Infra: note we need explicit approval to use cross-customer burst pools in EU region due to data residency. If they require isolated hardware, bursts must be reserved — significant cost.
Maria - Customer Success: flagged for compliance review. I'll start the audit checklist and get the customer's security contact.
Emma - Product: acceptance criteria for product backlog item:
- validated perf matrix on target GPU (p50/p95/p99 at baseline and peak)
- autoscale policy tested in staging with synthetic burst traffic
- rollout plan + canary + rollback steps
- cost estimate + contract terms for reserved vs burst capacity
- compliance signoff for VPC/audit logs
Emma - Product: owner suggestions: Sam for runtime perf, Li for infra + pooling, Sophie for runbook + sizing doc, Raj owns sales comms, Maria owns compliance queue. Timeline: perf spike test in 2 weeks, pricing draft by EOW next week.
deploy-bot: Created DP-2026-134: aurorahealth-dedicated-request (assignee: Emma).
Raj - Sales: I'll loop in AuroraSec and confirm whether soft-SLO is acceptable.
Sophie - Solutions Eng: I'll prepare a sizing worksheet (tokens/sec -> GPUs) and a short doc with tradeoffs. Link to example: https://redwood.internal/docs/dedicated-sizing.
Sam - Eng Runtime: tentative notes — if we need <200ms p95 at 1.2k qps, estimate: ~90 A10G GPUs with latency-optimized build (rough). Will run microbenchmarks once we have model binary.
Li - Eng Infra: pinging legal/finance for MRC modeling. if reserved 30 baseline + ability to reserve temp 70 for bursts, finance needs a proposal.
Emma - Product: next steps: Raj to confirm SLO flexibility + commitment length, Sophie to share sizing sheet by tomorrow, Sam to run perf tests once model artifacts arrive. We'll triage into product backlog once we have customer answers.
Maria - Customer Success: I'll schedule intro call with AuroraHealth security for next Tue.
Raj - Sales: noted. will update after security call. :thumbsup:
